name: Table lamp 'Model 61052' designed by Mauri Almari for Idman
description:
Table lamp 'Model 61052' designed by Mauri Almari in the 1950s, is a refined example of Finnish mid-century lighting where material and atmosphere are closely intertwined. The structure is composed of a slender brass frame, rising lightly from three looping feet that form a stable yet visually delicate base.

The shade is constructed from closely spaced vertical slats in rattan creating a permeable surface that filters the light. When illuminated, the construction produces a gentle interplay of light and shadow, casting linear patterns onto surrounding surfaces.

Mauri Almari (1907–1973) was a central figure in the development of Finnish lighting design during the post-war period. Through his work with Idman, he contributed to a body of designs characterised by clarity of form, technical precision and a sensitive use of materials. His lamps, like this example, balance functionality with an atmospheric quality that became a defining aspect of Scandinavian modern lighting.

name: Table lamp B-075, designed by Eje Ahlgren for Bergboms,
description:
Designed by Eje Ahlgren for the Swedish lighting manufacturer Bergboms, the 'B-075' table lamp is a distinctive example of Scandinavian mid-century lighting. Its softly rounded brass shade and balanced proportions give the lamp a sculptural presence, while the restrained construction reflects the period’s emphasis on clarity and function. A small rod at the top of the shade allows the light direction to be adjusted with ease, underscoring the practical thinking behind the design.

'B-075' belongs to a larger family of wall and floor lamps that share the same characteristic shade form, making it a versatile and coherent element within an interior. Developed during Ahlgren’s tenure as one of Bergboms’ principal designers in the 1950s and 1960s, the lamp sits within the company’s strong modernist tradition.

Bergboms was a key name in Scandinavian lighting, known for producing enduring designs and for earlier collaborations such as Greta Magnusson Grossman’s iconic 'Grasshopper' lamp.

name: Table lamp model  B 275 designed by Hans-Agne Jakobsson for Markaryd
description:
Designed by Hans-Agne Jakobsson, table lamp 'B-275' exemplifies his enduring commitment to soft, carefully controlled light and functional clarity. The model is distinguished by its adjustable, spherical shade, mounted on a gently curved brass arm that allows the light to be directed with precision. This articulation makes the lamp equally suited to focused task lighting and more atmospheric use, while maintaining the glare-free illumination for which Jakobsson is best known.

The globular shade is deliberately proportioned to conceal the light source, producing an even, diffused glow rather than direct brightness. This approach reflects Jakobsson’s broader design philosophy, shaped by the principles of Organic Modernism and influenced by figures such as Alvar Aalto and Poul Henningsen, where comfort and visual ease were placed above technical display.

Jakobsson’s background as an industrial designer, including his formative years at Orrefors, informed his sensitive understanding of materials and light. By the time he established his own studio in Markaryd in the early 1950s, he had developed a distinctive language in lighting design.

name: Table lamp model 2466 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
description:
An understated and timeless design, the model 2466 by Josef Frank is found in both a table lamp and floor lamp silhouette. The brass base structure is encased by lacquered metal often of a white, black or green tone with a range of different lampshades available. The simplicity of this design is emblematic of Josef Frank’s ‘lightweight and elegant’ ideals. He believed that "the home should be personal and comfortable” and emulated this in his warm and familiar designs.

name: Table lamp model B-090 for Bergboms
description:
Table lamp 'model B-090' was produced by Bergboms in Sweden during the 1960s and reflects the company’s characteristic emphasis on material quality and practical design. Executed in polished brass, the lamp is defined by its gently domed shade, which can be adjusted to direct the light according to use. A discreet pull cord switch is integrated beneath the shade, reinforcing the lamp’s straightforward and user-oriented construction.

Although the designer remains unknown, the lamp sits comfortably within Bergboms’ wider production during the mid-20th century. The firm was among Sweden’s most respected lighting manufacturers, recognised for its consistent use of durable materials and careful fabrication, often working closely with leading designers of the time.

Stamped.

name: Table lamp model 2434 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
description:
This table lamp, model 2434, was designed by Josef Frank in 1939 and produced by Svenskt Tenn. It is constructed with a circular brass base supporting a black-lacquered vertical stem. From the upper section, a flexible brass gooseneck arm extends, carrying a colourful conical shade that allows the light to be directed.

The use of brass and lacquered metal reflects Svenskt Tenn’s preference for durable materials suited to everyday interiors. The construction is straightforward and functional, with each component clearly defined and contributing to stability, adjustability, and controlled illumination.

Josef Frank, an Austrian-born architect and designer, became a central figure at Svenskt Tenn after beginning his collaboration with the firm in the mid-1930s. His work there encompassed furniture, textiles, and lighting, developed for modern domestic interiors rather than for exhibition purposes. Founded in Stockholm in 1924, Svenskt Tenn played a key role in shaping a human-centred approach to modern design, combining practicality with careful attention to proportion and material. Model 2434 fits within this context as a compact, functional table lamp intended for everyday use.

name: Table lamp for Nordiska Kompaniet
description:
This table lamp was purchased from Nordiska Kompaniet in the 1950s and features a tall, rectilinear form clad in hand-painted textile panels, signed “LJ”. Although the designer remains unidentified, the bold geometric composition—rendered in black, ochre, cream and yellow—reflects the abstract and modernist visual language that characterised Swedish design in the mid-20th century.

The lamp was likely made in Nordiska Kompaniet’s own workshops in Nyköping, Sweden, where furniture and lighting were produced for the department store throughout much of the 20th century. NK played a central role in shaping Swedish modernism, bringing together interior design and applied arts under one institution. Through collaborations with leading designers and artists, NK promoted a refined yet accessible vision of modern living.

name: Table lamp designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors
description: This lamp from 2004 exemplifies Per B. Sundberg’s idiosyncratic approach to combining image, function, and form. Created during his time at Orrefors, the piece features a cast glass base engraved with a detailed, comic-style scene: a jeep speeding through a rural setting, rendered in stark black lines. The imagery is unexpected in the context of glass design, where such narrative illustrations are uncommon, adding a layer of irony and visual tension. A red electrical cord is routed along the contours of the base, becoming part of the composition rather than being concealed. The vertical metal stem and white lampshade contrast with the visual density of the base, balancing the object’s playful irreverence with a restrained functional profile. This work sits at the intersection of art object and domestic utility, reflecting Sundberg’s continued interest in disrupting design conventions through both material and imagery.
